en: There is a big bookstore in front of the station.
why: An adjective comes before its noun, and が follows the noun.

en: I like listening to Japanese songs.
why: The verb comes before のが, and its object comes before the verb.

after: とてもおもしろかったです。
en: The movie I saw yesterday was very interesting.
why: {昨日|きのう}{見|み}た describes {映画|えいが}, and は marks the topic after it.

en: Mr. Tanaka is reading a new book now.
why: を comes after the noun, and the て-form comes right before います.

en: I like tea more than coffee.
why: The pattern is AよりBのほうが: after コーヒーより comes {紅茶|こうちゃ}のほうが, then {好|す}きです.

en: It will probably rain tomorrow, so please take an umbrella.
why: でしょう follows the verb, then から gives the reason.

en: I brush my teeth after eating.
why: The pattern is past verb + {後|あと}で.

en: I take a shower before going to bed.
why: {前|まえ}に follows the dictionary form, and ます needs the verb stem.

en: You must not smoke here.
why: The pattern is て-form + はいけません.

en: May I enter this room?
why: The pattern is て-form + もいいですか.

before: {日曜日|にちようび}は{映画|えいが}を{見|み}たり、
en: On Sundays I do things like watch movies and walk in the nearby park.
why: {近|ちか}くの describes {公園|こうえん}, and the たり verb comes last before します.

en: I want new shoes.
why: The adjective comes before the noun, and が comes before ほしい.

en: The ramen at this shop is cheap and tasty.
why: The て-form adjective links to the next adjective, which ends before です.

en: About how many minutes does it take to walk to the station?
why: ぐらい follows the amount, and かかります ends the question.

en: My house is not far from the station.
why: から follows the place, and {遠|とお}く comes before ありません.

en: You should ask the teacher.
why: The pattern is past verb + ほうがいい.

en: What is that white building?
why: {白|しろ}い describes ビル, and the question word comes before です.

en: There are three pens on the desk.
why: {机|つくえ}の{上|うえ} is one place phrase, so に comes after {上|うえ}.

en: Ms. Yamada is the person wearing glasses.
why: めがねをかけている describes {人|ひと}.

en: Please don't talk loudly on the train.
why: {大|おお}きい describes {声|こえ}, and ないでください needs the ない stem.

before: {去年|きょねん}の{夏|なつ}、{家族|かぞく}と
en: Last summer I went to a beautiful beach with my family.
why: きれいな describes {海|うみ}, and へ marks where you go.

en: My mother is good at cooking.
why: The pattern is verb + のが{上手|じょうず}です.

en: This is a watch I got from my father.
why: {父|ちち}にもらった describes {時計|とけい}.

en: Where did you buy that bag?
why: その comes before the noun, and ました needs the verb stem.

en: I want to drink cold water.
why: たい follows the verb stem, and が marks what you want.

en: Every day I get up at seven and go to the office.
why: The time takes に, then the て-form links to the next action.

en: It's raining, so let's go home by taxi.
why: {降|ふ}っている is the reason before から, and タクシー comes before で.

en: Please don't use a dictionary during the test.
why: テストの{時|とき} is one phrase, and ないでください needs the ない stem.

before: {山田|やまだ}さん、いっしょに
en: Ms. Yamada, would you like to eat lunch together?
why: The pattern is verb stem + ませんか.

en: My younger brother is sleeping in his room now.
why: {自分|じぶん}の describes {部屋|へや}, and で marks the place.

en: Who is that person?
why: あの comes before the noun, and だれ comes before ですか.

en: Studying Japanese is hard, but it is interesting.
why: {日本語|にほんご}の describes {勉強|べんきょう}, and the adjective comes before です.

en: I am not good at singing.
why: The pattern is Nが{上手|じょうず}ではありません.

en: May I open the window?
why: The pattern is Nを + て-form + もいいですか.

en: This book is one I borrowed from the library.
why: {図書館|としょかん}で{借|か}りた describes もの.

en: The weather is nice today, so let's take a walk.
why: {天気|てんき}がいい is the reason before から.

en: My younger sister is wearing the skirt she bought last week.
why: {先週|せんしゅう}{買|か}った describes スカート, and を follows it.

en: I want to drink something warm.
why: The pattern is {何|なに}か + adjective + もの.

en: Please tell me the way to the station.
why: {駅|えき}へ{行|い}く describes {道|みち}, and てください needs the て-form.

en: In Japan, people take off their shoes before entering a house.
why: The pattern is dictionary form + {前|まえ}に.

before: {私|わたし}は{音楽|おんがく}を
en: I do my homework while listening to music.
why: ながら follows the verb stem.

en: Who is coming to tomorrow's party?
why: あしたの describes パーティー, and だれが comes before the verb.

en: How much is one of these apples?
why: この comes before the noun, and いくら comes before ですか.

en: I'm a little tired, so let's drink some tea.
why: The reason comes before から, and を comes after お{茶|ちゃ}.

before: {私|わたし}は{夏休|なつやす}みに
en: I plan to go back to my country during summer vacation.
why: The pattern is dictionary form + つもりです.

en: I caught a cold, so I stayed home from school.
why: {風邪|かぜ}をひいた is the reason before から, and ました needs the stem.

after: コーヒーを{飲|の}みます。
en: Every morning my father drinks coffee while reading the newspaper.
why: ながら follows the verb stem.

after: は{私|わたし}の{妹|いもうと}です。
en: The girl over there is my younger sister.
why: あそこにいる describes {女|おんな}の{子|こ}.

en: How do you read this kanji?
why: The pattern is {何|なん}と + verb.

en: Tokyo is a lively city with many people.
why: にぎやかな must come right before {町|まち}.

after: よく{聞|き}いてください。
en: Please listen carefully to what the teacher says.
why: {先生|せんせい}の describes {話|はなし}, and を comes after it.

en: I didn't go anywhere yesterday.
why: The pattern is どこへも + negative verb.

en: There was nobody in the room.
why: The pattern is だれも + negative verb.

en: When is Mr. Yamada's birthday?
why: The month comes before the day.

before: {晩|ばん}ごはんの{後|あと}で、いっしょに
en: After dinner, shall we watch something fun on TV together?
why: The adjective comes before the noun, and ませんか needs the verb stem.

en: Which is faster, the train or the bus?
why: The pattern is AとBとどちらが～ですか.

en: What fruit do you like best?
why: The pattern is ～の{中|なか}で{何|なに}が{一番|いちばん}～ですか.

en: My younger sister has long hair and big eyes.
why: {長|なが}くて links the first part, and {目|め} must come before が{大|おお}きい.

en: I wash my hands after I get home.
why: The pattern is て-form + から.

en: Please turn right at the next corner.
why: The pattern is {角|かど}を{右|みぎ}に{曲|ま}がる.

en: My favorite sport is tennis.
why: {好|す}きな describes スポーツ, which is the topic with は.

en: It has been three years since I came to Japan.
why: The pattern is て-form + から.

en: I had no time this morning, so I didn't eat breakfast.
why: {時間|じかん}がなかった is the reason before から.

en: How much is that red sweater?
why: The adjective comes before the noun, and いくら comes before ですか.

en: I swim in the pool twice a week.
why: The pattern is {週|しゅう}に + number of times.

after: の{下|した}で{寝|ね}ています。
en: A black cat is sleeping under the chair.
why: The adjective comes before the noun, and いす comes before の{下|した}.

after: を{教|おし}えてください。
en: Teacher, please tell me the meaning of this word.
why: このことばの describes {意味|いみ}.

en: My older brother works at a bank.
why: で marks the place, and the て-form comes before います.

en: It got dark, so let's turn on the light.
why: The pattern is adjective く + なる.

en: Every night before bed I read a Japanese book.
why: The pattern is dictionary form + {前|まえ}に, and {日本語|にほんご}の describes {本|ほん}.

en: This cake isn't too sweet, and it's tasty.
why: The negative of {甘|あま}い is {甘|あま}くない, and its て-form links to the next adjective.

after: から、{遊|あそ}びに{行|い}きませんか。
en: There's no school tomorrow, so shall we go out and have fun?
why: {学校|がっこう}が{休|やす}みです is the reason before から.

after: {大|おお}きい{木|き}があります。
en: There is a big tree near the window.
why: The pattern is Nの{近|ちか}くに.

en: I am bad at writing kanji.
why: The pattern is verb + のが{下手|へた}です.

after: {日|ひ}は、{外|そと}へ{出|で}ません。
en: On snowy days, I don't go outside.
why: {雪|ゆき}が{降|ふ}っている describes {日|ひ}.

en: Mr. Tanaka is a tall, kind person.
why: The pattern is {背|せ}が{高|たか}い, and やさしい must come right before {人|ひと}.

en: Excuse me, where is the restroom?
why: The pattern is Nはどこにありますか.

before: これは{誕生日|たんじょうび}に
en: These are flowers I got from a friend on my birthday.
why: {友|とも}だちにもらった describes {花|はな}.

en: Next Monday is a holiday.
why: {来週|らいしゅう}の describes {月曜日|げつようび}.

before: {私|わたし}は{毎朝|まいあさ}、{家|いえ}から{駅|えき}
en: Every morning I go from my house to the station by bike.
why: The pattern is AからBまで, then {自転車|じてんしゃ}で before the verb.
